editor_note: A quiet Saturday led by a fresh FCPA guilty plea and a Minnesota benefits-fraud surge, with Dutch privacy enforcement policy and UK scrutiny of Meta's AI terms rounding out the day.

bottom_line.text: Ex-BizJet manager pleads guilty to Latin American bribery; re-test sales-agent and intermediary payment controls.
DOJ uncovers ~$30M Medicaid and SNAP fraud in Minnesota; check public-program billing controls.
Dutch AP publishes enforcement policy; review how it prioritises privacy cases if you process Dutch data.

cards.title: Former BizJet Sales Manager Pleads Guilty to Foreign Bribery
cards.summary: A former BizJet International sales manager pleaded guilty for his role in a scheme to pay bribes to government officials in Latin America to secure business for the company.
cards.impact: Individual FCPA pleas keep coming; review intermediary payments and sales-agent controls in high-risk markets, especially government-facing aviation and maintenance contracts.

cards.title: DOJ Fraud Division and Minnesota U.S. Attorney Uncover Nearly $30M in Benefits Fraud
cards.summary: The Justice Department's Fraud Division and the U.S. Attorney's Office in Minnesota announced a series of enforcement actions targeting fraud involving taxpayer-funded Medicaid and SNAP programs, totalling nearly $30 million.
cards.impact: Healthcare and benefits providers billing Medicaid should expect coordinated enforcement surges; test billing controls and False Claims Act exposure now.

cards.title: DOJ Final Rule Lets Firearms Licensees Use NICS for Employee Background Checks
cards.summary: The Justice Department issued a final rule authorizing federal firearms licensees to voluntarily use the FBI's NICS system to run background checks on certain current and prospective employees.
cards.impact: Firearms-sector employers should align screening policies with the rule and with FCRA, state ban-the-box and anti-discrimination requirements before adopting NICS checks.

cards.title: NLRB Reports Reduced Backlog in FY 2026 Case Processing Data
cards.summary: The NLRB said it reduced a substantial inherited backlog in FY 2026, with 21,587 charges and petitions filed, a 4.27% decrease from FY 2025, while demand for its services stays significant.
cards.impact: Labour charge volumes remain high; faster NLRB processing means unfair-labour-practice matters may resolve sooner, so keep labour-relations training and response plans current.

cards.title: HITRUST Launches IRIDX Risk-Scoring Subsidiary
cards.summary: HITRUST launched IRIDX, a wholly owned subsidiary that scores residual information risk and potential financial exposure, structured separately to protect the independence of its risk evaluations.
cards.impact: Third-party and cyber risk teams may see new quantified vendor scores; assess how such ratings would fit existing vendor due-diligence methodology.

cards.title: Dutch Data Protection Authority Publishes Its Enforcement Policy
cards.summary: The Dutch data protection authority (AP) has published its enforcement policy, setting out how it uses enforcement instruments when organisations do not comply with privacy rules.
cards.impact: Organisations processing Dutch personal data should read the policy to understand how the AP prioritises cases and chooses between warnings, orders and fines.

cards.title: UK Watchdog Probes Meta's AI Business Terms After Publisher Complaints
cards.summary: A UK watchdog will consider whether an update to Meta's terms and conditions on AI imposes unfair trading conditions, following an outcry from press publishers.
cards.impact: Businesses relying on platform terms for AI content use should monitor UK competition scrutiny of unilateral contract changes and review their own data-licensing terms.

cards.title: Dutch Government Warns of Privacy Risks in EU Kids Act
cards.summary: A Dutch government paper warns of privacy risks in the proposed EU Kids Act and says excessive reliance on parents could create inequalities between children.
cards.impact: Online services with child users should track the Kids Act negotiations; member-state privacy objections may reshape age-assurance and parental-consent obligations.

cards.source: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
cards.title: Canada and EU to Announce New Digital Cooperation Partnership
cards.summary: Canada's AI minister Evan Solomon and the European Commission's Henna Virkkunen will announce a new partnership to strengthen Canada–EU digital cooperation at the Canada–EU Summit.
cards.impact: Firms operating in both markets should watch for alignment on AI and digital rules that could ease or reshape cross-border AI governance obligations.
